newsitem.title: USA: Alternative Living to acquire Sterling.
newsitem.headline: Alternative Living to acquire Sterling.

text.p: Alternative Living Services Inc. said Thursday it has agreed to acquire Sterling House Corp. for about $170 million, creating the nation's largest operator of communities with living assistance and health care services.

The merged company will also be the nation's largest operator of residences for individuals with Alzheimer's disease and other memory impairments, and have annualized revenues of more than $115 million.
Under the definitive agreement, Brookfield, Wis.-based Alternative Living will issue 1.1 common shares for each Sterling House common share in a tax-free pooling of interests.
Alternative Living will assume all the outstanding debt of Sterling House, which is based in Wichita, Kan.
Sterling House's stock jumped $4.06 to $22.31, while Alternative Living fell 12.5 cents to $21.50 on the American Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.
After the merger, Assisted Living will have about 18.5 million common shares outstanding worth about $400 million, based on current prices, it said.
Holders of about 46 percent of Sterling House shares outstanding have agreed to vote in favour of the merger, the company said.
Assisted and Sterling have granted each other options to buy 19.9 percent of the other company's stock if the deal falls through under certain circumstances.
The deal, which has been unanimously approved by the boards of both companies, is expected to close in the fourth quarter.
The combined company will have 178 residences in 19 states that can accommodate about 8,000 residents, and 65 residences under construction and 81 in development.
